# Replace scan.py find-workitem with native wl CLI lookup in audit prompts

## Problem statement

The audit SCANNING blocks and docs currently recommend
`scan.py find-workitem <id>` for worklog lookups (wired in by
SA-0MSBR0SRK0035HB1; guidance refined by SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI).
`scan.py find-workitem` wraps `wl search <id> --json` plus an exact-id
post-filter. Once the wl CLI gains tolerant ID resolution (the ContextHub
feature below), audit agents should use native wl commands for worklog
lookups and `scan.py find-workitem` can be retired.

## Blocked by

- **WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E** — "Add tolerant work-item ID resolution to `wl show`
  (exact-first, unique substring fallback, ambiguity error) for agent tool
  use" — feature request in the **ContextHub** repository
  (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`), created 2026-08-11.

This item MUST NOT start until that feature lands in the installed wl CLI
(the exact-match `wl show` today cannot resolve partial/truncated IDs, which
is why the scan.py wrapper exists). Cross-project dependency — recorded here
as a blocker; not a `wl dep` edge (different worklog DBs).

## Substring-matching guidance (researched — use ONLY the optimal command)

The canonical substring-matching primitive is **`wl list <term> --json`**:
case-insensitive substring match over id/title/description, JSON mode returns
all matches, supports `-n/--number` and filters (see `src/commands/list.ts`
in ContextHub).

`wl search <keywords> --json` is full-text search (FTS, token/prefix-based) —
**not** a substring matcher — and must NOT be presented as one.

Exact / unique-ID resolution: **`wl show <id> --json`** (tolerant once
WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E lands; `scan.py find-workitem <id>` interim).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All SCANNING blocks in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
   (`_PHASE1_SCANNING_BLOCK`, phase2_child, phase2_batch, phase2_deep) direct
   worklog lookups to native wl commands only:
   - substring matching: `wl list <term> --json`
   - exact/unique-ID resolution: `wl show <id> --json`
2. The dual recommendation "`wl search <keywords> --json` or
   `wl list <term> --json` for substring matching" (introduced by
   SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI) is corrected to the single optimal command
   **`wl list <term> --json`** everywhere it appears (audit_runner.py +
   docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md), per the research note above.
3. `scan.py find-workitem` is removed (subcommand, its tests, and references
   in audit-grep-scan-patterns.md) OR deprecated with a clear notice — the
   decision is documented in a comment; `scan.py search-code` and
   `scan.py list-files` remain unchanged.
4. docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md and docs/dev/audit-grep-scan-patterns.md
   (incl. the P9 replacement recipe) updated to the native commands.
5. Full project test suite passes (canonical PATH with `~/.local/bin`).
6. Related docs (README, wiki/docs-site entries, code comments, scan.py
   module docstring) updated; no stale `scan.py find-workitem` guidance
   remains.

## Out of scope

- No changes to `scan.py search-code` / `list-files` (bounded code search).
- No changes to the wl CLI itself — tracked in ContextHub WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E.
- No changes to audit verdict semantics or prompt structure beyond the
  worklog-lookup guidance lines.

## Related work

- SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI — removed stale `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` grep
  guidance from audit prompts (completed, this item's precursor).
- SA-0MSBR0SRK0035HB1 — wired scan.py guidance into audit prompts (the
  guidance this item replaces).
- SA-0MSAEJCP7002LTIM / SA-0MSBSOAEM0078LAO — scan hygiene parents.
data.title: Replace scan.py find-workitem with native wl CLI lookup in audit prompts (blocked by ContextHub WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E)

# R6 — Report provider errors separately from parse failures

**Parent:** SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL (RCA: audit Phase 1/Phase 2 reliability)
**Discovered-from:** SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 (audit, 2026-09-15).

## Problem

Provider errors are conflated with parse failures in reporting and analysis.
The 2026-09-15 corpus shows `Pi provider error` 15 (generic `provider error`
75) against a `parse_failure` label that is itself unreliable (see R1). This
prevents distinguishing a flaky model/provider from a schema-contract problem.

## Desired change

Use the corrected taxonomy from R1 to report provider errors distinctly, with
per-run counts (feeding R7).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Audit reports and debug entries distinguish provider errors from parse
   failures (no conflation); provider errors retain their retry provenance.
2. Provider-error counts are surfaced per run (see R7's summary line).
3. Tests cover both classifications, including a provider error that succeeds
   on retry.
4. Full project test suite passes.

## Dependencies

- Depends on **R1** (reason taxonomy) for accurate classification.

## Constraints

- UK English.
- No verdict-semantics change.

# R7 — Emit a per-run audit reliability summary

**Parent:** SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL (RCA: audit Phase 1/Phase 2 reliability)
**Discovered-from:** SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 (audit, 2026-09-15).

## Problem

Assessing audit reliability currently requires log archaeology across
`~/.audit_debug/**` and the worklog export (the RCA for
SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL needed bespoke scripts). There is no single per-run
signal an operator can read to see how healthy an audit was.

## Desired change

Emit one machine-greppable reliability summary per `audit_runner.py issue`
run, so future RCAs and dashboards do not need log archaeology.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each `audit_runner.py issue` run emits exactly one summary line (stderr
   and/or appended to the report) with stable, documented keys: calls,
   parse_ok, parse_failed, timeouts, child_skips, provider_errors,
   concurrency_waits, elapsed_seconds.
2. The summary format is documented in `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.
3. Tests cover the summary formatting and key stability.
4. The summary is available even when the run ends early (timeout/abort),
   where possible.
5. Full project test suite passes.

## Dependencies

- Depends on **R1** for accurate parse/provider counts; **R6** for provider
  totals.

## Constraints

- UK English.
- Must not print secrets/credentials; counts only.

## Summary
A resumed run detects budget-exceeded children in the checkpoint and re-audits them without re-running completed phases.

2. Completed phases from the prior run are skipped.

- On resume (checkpoint.is_resuming == True), identify children marked as budget-exceeded.

- The resume logic should distinguish between:

# implement.py finish leaves local dev behind after pushing to remote dev

Counterpart of the AI_Hell discovery report **AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB**
(`discovered-from:AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB`). The defect is in agent infrastructure in this
repository — `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`. The full discovery context (observed
commits, parent run, workaround) is on the AI_Hell report; this item is the actionable fix.

## Headline

After `implement.py finish <child>` pushes the child's branch to `origin/dev`, the main
checkout's local `dev` branch is left one or more commits behind, so the next
`implement.py parent <epic>` / `implement.py start <child>` creates the following child's
worktree from a stale base and is missing the previous sibling's files.

## Problem statement

`phase_finish` restores the main checkout to the parent branch **before** pushing the
just-committed branch to `origin dev`:

- Step 7 — `_restore_repo_state(repo_root)` runs `git checkout dev` then `git pull origin dev`
  (local `dev` fast-forwards only to the **pre-push** remote tip).
- Step 8 — `git_push_to_dev(repo_root, branch)` runs
  `git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev` (the new commit lands on the remote after the pull).

Local `dev` is therefore left behind. `git_worktree_add()` forks each child from the **local**
parent branch (`git worktree add --track -b <branch> <worktree> dev`) and `phase_start`
performs no fetch, so every subsequent child starts from the stale base.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running the parent/epic flow (`implement.py parent`).
- **Operators / orchestrators** relying on the parent flow being self-consistent without
  manual `git fetch` / `git merge` steps.

### Example user stories

- As an implementation agent, after `finish` reports "commit pushed to dev", I want the main
  checkout's local `dev` to contain that commit, so the next `parent`/`start` child worktree
  includes my just-finished sibling's files.
- As an operator, I want the parent flow to never create a child from a stale base, so I do
  not have to diagnose phantom build errors or risk lost/duplicated work.

## Observed (from AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB)

- F2 (`AH-0MUBYU600004YU4T`) `finish` pushed `91538d0` to `origin/dev`; local `dev` stayed at
  `1920e65`.
- The F3 worktree (`AH-0MUBYXR280018HST`) was created from local `dev` `1920e65` and could not
  resolve `../powerups/collectAnimation` (added by F2) until local `dev` was manually
  fast-forwarded and merged into the worktree.
- Workaround applied by hand during the parent `AH-0MUAYB3OU0087H9W` run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Post-push local parent sync.** After a successful push in `phase_finish`, the
  main checkout's local parent branch (`dev`) is at least as advanced as the pushed tip when
  it is safe to fast-forward (local `dev` == pushed commit == `origin/dev`).
- [ ] **AC2 — Safe-skip semantics.** When the update is not safe (dirty main checkout, other
  branch/detached, or local `dev` diverged), `finish` does not force it, loses no local
  commits, and does not fail. The skip is reported and the repo remains recoverable.
- [ ] **AC3 — Children never start from a stale base.** `parent`/`start` refresh the parent
  branch (`fetch` + fast-forward) before `git worktree add`, or fork from
  `origin/<parent_branch>` after a fetch.
- [ ] **AC4 — Regression tests.** A focused regression test (e.g.
  `tests/test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py`) covers AC1–AC3; existing
  `tests/test_implement_*.py` still pass.
- [ ] **AC5 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation updated** (`skill/implement/SKILL.md`, code comments, README and
  any relevant docs-site entries) for the new post-push sync and safe-skip semantics.

## Constraints

- No new runtime dependencies; reuse stdlib and the existing `run_cmd` / `git_*` helpers.
- Never force-update a branch with local commits; prefer `--ff-only`.
- Must not regress worktree-based finish (worktree is removed before the push).
- Remote-unreachable / dirty-checkout paths degrade gracefully (report, do not fail a finish
  that already pushed successfully).
- All written output in UK English.

## Existing state

- `DEFAULT_PARENT_BRANCH = "dev"`.
- `_restore_repo_state(repo_root)` → `git checkout dev`; `git pull origin dev`.
- `git_push_to_dev(cwd, branch)` → `git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev`.
- `git_worktree_add(branch, worktree_path, parent_branch)` → `git worktree add --track -b ...`;
  `phase_start` does no fetch.
- `phase_finish` order: remove worktree → `_restore_repo_state` → `git_push_to_dev`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — reorder/guard the post-push local parent sync and
  refresh the parent branch in `phase_start` before `git_worktree_add`.
- `tests/test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py` — new regression test for AC1–AC3.
- `tests/test_implement_parent_recursion.py`, `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py` —
  extend parent-flow coverage (fresh base for the next child).
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — document the post-push local parent sync and safe-skip semantics.

## Related work
